context: Two packages, two different CI defects, both caused by a runner-inappropriate invocation rather than by the tests. Predicted baseline failure: the agent spots `--watchAll` because the flag names the problem, but leaves the `web` script as bare `vitest` - which is also watch mode and is the actual cause of the hang, and reads as correct because it does not carry a watch-looking flag. The OOM fix is likewise a worker-count question rather than a memory setting, and an agent that does not know Jest defaults to one worker per core tends to reach for NODE_OPTIONS heap tuning instead.

checklist.name: The Vitest package runs a single pass
checklist.description: `web`'s test command is `vitest run` (or passes `--run`). Leaving it as bare `vitest` scores zero - that is watch mode and is the cause of the hang, regardless of anything else the answer fixes. Adding `--watch=false` is acceptable.

checklist.name: The Jest package runs a single pass
checklist.description: `--watchAll` is gone from `api`'s test command. Replacing it with `--watch` scores zero; both are watch modes.

checklist.name: Worker count is pinned for the two-core runner
checklist.description: The Jest run pins concurrency, e.g. `--maxWorkers=2` (or an equivalent cap on the Vitest side if the same problem is addressed there). Raising the Node heap via NODE_OPTIONS instead scores at most half: it may postpone the OOM but leaves one worker per core spawned on a two-core box, which is the documented cause. Doing nothing about concurrency scores zero.

checklist.name: Machine-readable results per package
checklist.description: Each package emits a JUnit XML (or equivalent structured) report to a file - Jest via a JUnit reporter, Vitest via `--reporter=junit --outputFile=...`. Printing a more verbose console reporter scores zero: the task asks for something the reporting tooling can read, not a nicer log.

checklist.name: Result files are uploaded and survive a failing job
checklist.description: The workflow uploads the report artefact with `if: always()` (or `if: failure()`), and the artefact name is distinct per matrix entry so the two packages do not collide. Uploading without a condition scores at most half; not uploading at all scores zero.

checklist.name: Jest runs in CI mode
checklist.description: The Jest invocation passes `--ci`, so a missing snapshot fails the run instead of being written and silently committed later.

checklist.name: No test files changed
checklist.description: MUST NOT modify or add any test file. Both failures are invocation problems; editing tests to work around them scores zero.

checklist.name: Both packages still run
checklist.description: The matrix still covers `web` and `api`. Dropping a package to make the job pass scores zero.
